I have indeed looked at the Nures, and was hesitant about claiming them for the following reasons:

  1. The Nures are innately violent and seek to kill other creatures out of their nature, thus weakening their ability for diplomacy and limiting interactions with other races (should that ever become a thing. As far as I could tell, their free will gives them the choice of what to kill, but the race in general has violence and murder as an ingrained trait.)

  2. Nures are only capable of projecting fear, while fear is useful, it seems to align with their nature as hunters, predators of all life on Gaea, as was their primary intended purpose. Their exceptional physical power tends to lead itself to war almost inevitably if I were to try to write them according to their natures.

  3. They might be slightly difficult to tell tragedies of, especially since they seem to be thriving quite well without having to suffer a history of hardship.

  4. I want to make a race that will hopefully encourage more race interactions, and the Nures, by their nature, would probably (for the most part) not co-exist as much with other races as they would continuously cull the races they share spaces with.

In short, a race of shape-shifting fear-inducing killing machines might not exactly get along too well with other races in terms of interactions, and lack subtlety and manipulation. The strength of their physical forms and abilities, as well as their urges tend to favour conflict almost inevitably with other races. While I did see many aspects of the Nures most interesting, I don't quite think they can be shaped into a strong semblance of the race I envisioned without some pretty significant changes to their core aspects (as far as I can see them).
